title: Accepted but Wrong: Silent Failures of LLM Code Repairs after API Migrations
summary: After an API migration, LLM-repaired code can run cleanly and still be wrong; one edge input written from the release note catches most wrong repairs that a typical-input check ships.

title: Signed but Not Safe: Requirement Integrity in Multi-Agent LLM Handoffs
summary: Signing agent handoffs stops tampering in transit, but one injected line before signing gets through: the signature then authenticates a corrupted requirement list.

title: Humanized but Still True? Auditing Facts and Detection in AI-Text Humanizers
summary: Commercial AI-text humanizers change or drop checkable facts (numbers, dates, names, quotes) in 35–65% of documents while trying to evade detectors.

title: Evidence-Guided Recovery for AI Agents with Ambiguous Tool Outcomes and Partial Execution
summary: Recovering AI agents after tool timeouts leave outcomes ambiguous: evidence-guided planning certifies safe completions that evidence prompting misses.

title: Verifying Text-to-SQL Queries under Changing Business Semantics
summary: A Text-to-SQL query can run correctly and still be wrong after business definitions change; obligation-guided counterexample checking finds more of these discrepancies.

title: Do Multimodal Models Decide Consistently on Equivalent Optical Spectra?
summary: Multimodal models change their answers on the same optical spectrum depending on whether it is shown as a table or a plot, in nanometers or electronvolts.

title: Payroll Fraud Detection in Synthetic HR/ERP Graphs: An Inductive Comparison of Rules, Path Features, and Graph Neural Networks
summary: On synthetic HR/ERP graphs, boosted trees on chained-join path features beat graph neural networks at finding hidden employee–payee links.
